fig1_galilean_worldlines.svg: Worldlines of three objects (x horizontal, absolute time t vertical) in the lab frame S and in a frame S' boosted at V=0.5, mapped by the module's Galilean transform x' = x - V t. Every slope shifts by -V, so the object moving at V becomes a vertical (at-rest) worldline in S'; time is unchanged.
fig2_velocity_addition.svg: Combining a fixed u=0.5c with a second velocity v. The Galilean rule w=u+v (orange) is a straight line that overshoots c, while Einstein's relativistic addition (blue) saturates at the dashed light line c. The two agree only at small v/c, where Galilean relativity is the low-speed limit.
